# Ostadix-lang

> Ostadix-lang (O-lang) is a polyglot orchestration language where every
> expression carries its own interpreter as part of its syntax. A block written
> as `LANG^( ... )_LANG` is evaluated by that language's backend, and all
> results flow through one canonical value type, OValue. AI agents can use O as
> a single primary language while delegating each subtask to whichever hosted
> language (Python, Bash, SQL, Rust, JavaScript, ...) solves it best.

Key facts for agents:

- File extension: `.O` (hosted orchestration) and `.oc` (O-core native systems language).
- Run a program: `O program.O` or `o run program.O` (Rust edition; build with
  `./setup.sh --minimal`).
- Machine-readable output: `O --json program.O` prints one JSON object on
  stdout: `{"ok":true,"value":...,"type":...,"elapsed_ms":...}` on success, or
  `{"ok":false,"stage":"parse"|"eval","error":"..."}` on failure (exit code 1).
- Syntax check without executing: `O --check program.O` (combine with `--json`).
- Inline evaluation: `O --eval '<O source>'` or `O -e '<O source>'`.
- Blocks: `python^( ... )_python`, `bash^( ... )_bash`, `sql^( ... )_sql`, etc.
  Opener and closer tags must match exactly.
- Persistent state: `python[0]^( ... )_python[0]` reuses one Python process for
  every block marked `[0]`; unmarked blocks are ephemeral. Generated
  `python[*]^( ... )_python[*]` blocks request fresh linker-isolated execution
  without minting a persistent actor identity.
- Values: a Python block returns whatever it assigns to `__oval_result__`;
  inline backends (`html`, `markdown`, `text`) return their spliced body.
- Bindings: `let name = LANG^( ... )_LANG` then reference `$name` inside any
  later block. Escape a literal dollar sign as `\$`.
- Quoting: `quote^( ... )_quote` captures unevaluated O source; `O.eval(expr)`
  inside Python evaluates it (homoiconicity).
- Fabric V1 can execute only the admitted M2 pure renderer profile on an
  explicitly selected authenticated `o-node`. The result is a bounded
  provisional candidate; only the coordinator may validate, publish, or settle
  it. Current evidence uses two real processes on one host and makes no
  physical-multinode, distinct-kernel, or heterogeneous-architecture claim.

## Docs

- [AI agent guide](docs/AI_GUIDE.md): how AI systems should write, check, and run O programs
- [Language specification](SPEC.md): grammar, evaluation semantics, OValue, backend protocol, registered languages
- [README](README.md): setup, all editions (Rust, C17, Python reference), tooling
- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md): runtime and compiler internals
- [O-core](docs/OCORE.md): the statically typed freestanding native language
- [Ostadix World constitution](docs/OSTADIX_WORLD.md): native Alpha target,
  G0-G13 dependency ladder, evidence boundaries, and implementation program
- [Hosted World reference profile](docs/HOSTED_WORLD_REFERENCE_PROFILE.md):
  non-qualifying simulator/oracle boundary retained for development
- [Hosted Placement V6](docs/HOSTED_PLACEMENT_V6.md): target descriptors,
  warrants, the local signed registry, and the bounded direct-node preview
- [OIR Execution Fabric V1](docs/OIR_EXECUTION_FABRIC_V1.md): frozen M2 pure
  records, additive authenticated M3 transport, coordinator-only graph authority,
  evidence, and exact nonclaims
- [M3 authenticated pure remote-execution design](docs/M3_AUTHENTICATED_PURE_REMOTE_EXECUTION_DESIGN.md):
  unchanged M2 types, additive M3 types, dependency split, and same-host proof
